signalCoverage.description: Signal coverage in two groups. `recovery` covers the freshness of sleep/HRV/resting-HR/stress and vendor composites; `training` covers whether every session in the last 7 days carried a training load. A gap in either lowers confidence, and they are kept apart so a caller can tell which half is unread. The load is the vendor's own effort figure and is used as it stands — RPE is carried as evidence but is not a term in any sum, so a source that never reports one is not penalised.

signalWriters.description: Where each signal came from and who wrote it, and when it was last written. Keyed by canonical signal name. A signal being listed does not make it current: compare its `latest` against the others to see a device that stopped writing.

sources.description: What the caller said this signal came from, sorted — the `source` field on each reading. Empty when no reading of this signal stated one.

writers.description: Devices or apps that wrote this signal, sorted. Empty when the connector recorded none.

latest.description: ISO 8601 of the most recent reading of this signal.

baselineEstablishing.description: True when the vendor says its own baseline for this signal is still forming — Garmin marks a daily HRV reading ONBOARDING until it has enough nights to compare against. The reading is used at full value and no penalty is applied to it, because inventing one would be a threshold with no source. Absent means no vendor flagged it, not that the baseline is established: that is not something we would know.

proposal.description: Present only when the caller proposed an alternative. The verdict on that proposal, judged against the ceiling rules 1-7 established — never against a threshold invented for proposals.

violations.description: Empty when accepted. Each entry names the axis that failed and by how much.

decisionBasis.description: What the decision stands on. `governingRule` is the rule the decision is attributed to, carrying the reading that triggered it (`measured`), the thresholds it was compared against, and the provenance of those thresholds: `sources` for published work supporting them, `supportingLiterature` for work supporting the rule's direction but explicitly not its number, `contested` for published objections to the method, and `limitations`. `basis` separates the two kinds of threshold. external_metric: the quantity is defined outside Evidra, so literature can speak to it. internal_composite: the threshold cuts a score Evidra computes from weights it chose, so no publication can support it and `sources` is empty by design, not by omission. Most rules are internal_composite. `appliedRules` lists every rule that fired, compact, with `applied: false` where a rule triggered but could not act. `policies` names the arbitration and combination policies by id.

libraryVersion.description: The version of the rule library the thresholds and their provenance came from. Moves when a threshold or a citation changes.

engineVersion.description: The version of the code that applied those rules — arbitration order, how effects combine, how a condition is evaluated. Moves independently of the library, and neither is the version of the installed extension.

governingRule.description: Null only when no rule fired at all — the session ran as planned with nothing to report.

appliedRules.description: Ordered by the arbitration policy: governing rule first, overruled rules after.
